questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. Research is ongoing to answer this question.

B. COVID vaccines have only been developed in the past few months, therefore it’s too early to say how long the COVID-19 vaccines will protect us.

C. The fact is we’re still learning how strong this protection is, and how long it lasts.

D. However, it’s encouraging that available data suggest that most people who recover from COVID-19 develop an immune response that provides at least some period of protection against reinfection.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**B, C, A, D**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage.
 
• **Statement B** is the opening sentence of the passage it introduces the theme of the passage which is **Covid-19 vaccines and their efficacy.**
 
• **Statement C **is the second sentence of the passage as it tries the answer the question raised in the first line about **how long the vaccine will protect us** is still being studied.
 
• **Statement A **is the third sentence of the passage as it states the question of the duration of protection that vaccine offers can be only **answered by research.**
 
• **Statement D** is the last sentence of the passage as it begins with the **conjunctive adverb** "however" which is often used to introduce contrasting information. In this sentence, we can see that people who recover from COVID-19 develop an** immune response **against the virus. This is in contrast to other sentences of the passage which talked about the protection offered by the **vaccine and its duration**.

Hence, the correct sequence is** B, C, A, D.**

**The correct passage is: B.** COVID vaccines have only been developed in the past few months, therefore it’s too early to say how long the COVID-19 vaccines will protect us. **C**. The fact is we’re still learning how strong this protection is, and how long it lasts. **A**. Research is ongoing to answer this question. **D**. However, it’s encouraging that available data suggest that most people who recover from COVID-19 develop an immune response that provides at least some period of protection against reinfection.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

On ______ of the river, I could see lush green corn fields.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**both sides**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Let's look at why the other options are incorrect.
 
• In option 2, "**other sides**" is an **irregular usage**. We don't say or write other sides of the river.
 
• In option 3, "**either**" is used when an **alternative **or choice is before us.
 
• In the given sentence, since there is no choice it would be incorrect to use "**either sides**".
 
• In option 4, "**other side**" seems to be missing an article 'the' before the phrase.
 
• In option 1, the sentence is grammatically and semantically correct.

**The complete sentence is**: *On **both sides **__of the river, I could see lush green corn fields*.

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1**.

• There are a few rules to keep in mind when changing a sentence from direct speech to indirect speech.
 
• In the given sentence, the reporting verb "**said to**"(direct) changes to **"told" **in indirect speech.
 
• The first-person pronouns in direct speech such as **I **and **me **will change to third-person pronouns such as** he/she** and **him/her** respectively..

• If I **had** studied, I **would've passed** the exam.
 
 
 
• The tense form in third conditional sentences, when changed from Direct to Indirect, doesn't change.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.
